claim: LMO2 is essential to maintain the ability of progenitors to differentiate into T-cell lineage in mice.
source: LMO2 is essential to maintain the ability of progenitors to differentiate into T-cell lineage in mice
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental approaches including gain-of-function and loss-of-function experiments.

claim: Two murine Ebf1-deficient pro-B cell lines were established, with and without T-lineage potential.
source: Here, we established two murine Ebf1-deficient pro-B cell lines, with and without T-lineage potential.
evidence: The establishment of these cell lines is described in the methods and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Pro-B cells without T-lineage potential expressed lower levels of Lmo2 compared to those with T-lineage potential.
source: The latter expressed lower levels of Lmo2
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR and intracellular staining shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Ectopic expression of Lmo2 restored T-lineage potential in pro-B cells that lacked this capacity.
source: their potential was restored via ectopic expression of Lmo2
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1D showing that Lmo2 transduction enables differentiation.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of Lmo2 resulted in the loss of T-lineage potential.
source: Conversely, the CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of Lmo2 resulted in the loss of the T-lineage potential.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2 where sgRNA-mediated deletion of Lmo2 prevents T-cell differentiation.

claim: Introduction of Bcl2 rescued massive cell death of Notch-stimulated pro-B cells without efficient LMO2-driven Bcl11a expression.
source: Introduction of Bcl2 rescued massive cell death of Notch-stimulated pro-B cells without efficient LMO2-driven Bcl11a expression
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3B showing reduced cell death with Bcl2 overexpression.

claim: Bcl2 introduction was not sufficient to retain T-lineage potential in pro-B cells lacking LMO2.
source: but was not sufficient to retain their T-lineage potential
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3C where Bcl2-transduced pro-B(-) cells fail to progress to CD25+ stage.

claim: Pro-B cells without T-lineage potential failed to activate Tcf7 due to DNA methylation.
source: Pro-B cells without T-lineage potential failed to activate Tcf7 due to DNA methylation
evidence: This is demonstrated by bisulfite sequencing in Figure 5B showing high methylation at the Tcf7 locus in pro-B(-) cells.

claim: Tcf7 transduction restored T-lineage differentiation capacity in pro-B cells lacking this potential.
source: Tcf7 transduction restored this capacity
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C where Tcf7 introduction enables differentiation to CD25+ stage.

claim: Direct binding of LMO2 to the Bcl11a and Tcf7 loci was observed.
source: Moreover, direct binding of LMO2 to the Bcl11a and Tcf7 loci was observed.
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: LMO2 ensures survival of pro-B cells through activation of the Bcl11a/Bcl2 pathway.
source: Furthermore, LMO2 ensures survival of pro-B cells through the activation of the Bcl11a/Bcl2 pathway
evidence: This is supported by data showing Lmo2 regulates Bcl11a expression (Figure 3A) and Bcl2 rescues cell death (Figure 3B).

claim: LMO2 contributes to maintaining the accessibility of the Tcf7 locus.
source: contributes to maintaining the accessibility of the Tcf7 locus
evidence: This is demonstrated by DNA methylation analysis (Figure 5B) and H3K4-3Me ChIP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: Notch signaling primarily determines T-cell fate.
source: Notch signaling primarily determines T-cell fate.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The molecular mechanisms underlying the maintenance of T-lineage potential in pre-thymic progenitors remain unclear.
source: However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the maintenance of T-lineage potential in pre-thymic progenitors remain unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap that motivates the study.

claim: Hematopoietic stem cells have the ability to self-renew and differentiate into all blood cell types.
source: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) have the ability to self-renew and differentiate into all blood cell types.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Doulatov et al., 2012; Kosan and Godmann, 2016.

claim: HSCs differentiate into hematopoietic progenitor cells and then into mature blood cells, gradually losing their potential.
source: HSCs begin to differentiate into various lineage cells, gradually losing their potential to become their descendants, hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs), and then differentiate into mature blood cells (Doulatov et al., 2012; Kosan and Godmann, 2016).
evidence: This describes the established model of hematopoietic differentiation.

claim: Cell fate decisions in hematopoietic cells are controlled by continuous interactions between environmental influences and intrinsic cellular mechanisms.
source: Cell fate decisions in hematopoietic cells are controlled by continuous interactions between environmental influences and intrinsic cellular mechanisms, such as transcription factor networks and epigenetic regulation (Wilson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Wilson et al., 2009.

claim: T-cell lineage specification requires the specialized environment of the thymus.
source: In the process of specification from HPCs, only the T-cell lineage requires a specialized environment of the thymus
evidence: This is established knowledge about T-cell development.

claim: Notch signaling is induced by the interaction of Notch1 on immigrant cells and delta-like 4 (Dll4) on thymic epithelium.
source: where the immigrant cells receive Notch signaling induced by the interaction of Notch1 on the immigrant cells and a Notch ligand, delta-like 4 (Dll4), on the thymic epithelium, which determines their fate to the T-cell lineage (Radtke et al., 1999; Hozumi et al., 2008; Koch et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: Several transcription factors contribute to the acquisition of T-cell identity, including TCF1, E2A, HEB, PU.1, GATA3, Bcl11b, and Runx family members.
source: In addition, several transcription factors contribute to the acquisition of T-cell identity, including TCF1 (encoded by Tcf7), basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) factors, E2A and HEB, PU.1, GATA3, Bcl11b, and Runx family members, all of which are essential for T-cell development in the thymus (Hosokawa and Rothenberg, 2021; Hosokawa et al., 2021a; Hosokawa et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from recent reviews.

claim: Tcf7 is one of the earliest Notch-activated genes and plays a critical role in Notch-mediated initiation of the T-lineage program.
source: Among them, one of the earliest Notch-activated genes, Tcf7, plays a critical role in Notch-mediated initiation of the T-lineage program (Weber et al., 2011; Johnson et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Weber et al., 2011 and Johnson et al., 2018.

claim: T-cell lineage commitment occurs in double-negative thymocytes at the transition from DN2 to DN3 stages.
source: The coordinated action of these environmental and intrinsic factors completes the commitment to T-cell lineage in double-negative (DN; CD4−CD8−) thymocytes at the transition from the DN2 to DN3 stages (Yui and Rothenberg, 2014; Hosokawa and Rothenberg, 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yui and Rothenberg, 2014 and Hosokawa and Rothenberg, 2021.

claim: LMO2 gene is located near the breakpoint of the chromosomal translocation t(11;14)(p13;q11) in human T-ALL.
source: LMO2 gene is located near the breakpoint of the chromosomal translocation t(11;14) (p13;q11) in human T-ALL (Boehm et al., 1991; Royer-Pokora et al., 1991)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Boehm et al., 1991 and Royer-Pokora et al., 1991.

claim: LMO2 functions as a bridging factor in large transcriptional complexes with several DNA-binding and adaptor proteins.
source: LMO2 has been thought to function as a bridging factor in large transcriptional complexes with several DNA-binding and adaptor proteins (TAL1/SCL, E2A, GATA1, and Ldb1) (Wadman et al., 1997; Grütz et al., 1998; El Omari et al., 2013; Layer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: Deletion of Lmo2 in mice causes embryonic lethality due to embryonic erythropoiesis deficiency around 10 days post-fertilization.
source: Although deletion of Lmo2 in mice causes embryonic lethality due to embryonic erythropoiesis deficiency around 10 days post-fertilization (Yamada et al., 1998)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yamada et al., 1998.

claim: Conditional disruption of Lmo2 in T-lineage committed pro-T stages results in normal T-cell development in the thymus.
source: conditional disruption of Lmo2 in T-lineage committed pro-T stages results in normal T-cell development in the thymus (McCormack et al., 2003)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from McCormack et al., 2003.

claim: LMO2 is dispensable for T-cell development after T-lineage commitment.
source: indicating that LMO2 is dispensable for T-cell development after T-lineage commitment
evidence: This is inferred from the McCormack et al., 2003 study showing normal T-cell development after conditional Lmo2 deletion.

claim: Gene therapy trials using retrovirus-mediated introduction of the common cytokine receptor gamma chain in X-SCID patients resulted in T-cell leukemia due to retroviral insertion at the LMO2 locus.
source: It is well known that the recent gene therapy trials using retrovirus-mediated introduction of the common cytokine receptor gamma chain (γc; CD132) in X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency (X-SCID) patients resulted in the development of T-cell leukemia due to retroviral insertion at the LMO2 locus (Hacein-Bey-Abina et al., 2003; Hacein-Bey-Abina et al., 2008; Howe et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: Transgenic overexpression of Lmo2 in various murine tissues only results in T-cell leukemia.
source: Moreover, transgenic overexpression of Lmo2 in various murine tissues only results in T-cell leukemia, indicating its involvement exclusively in T-cell malignancies when abnormally expressed (Neale et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Neale et al., 1995.

claim: Lmo2 is more highly expressed in HSCs and HPCs than in mature blood cells.
source: On the other hand, Lmo2 is more highly expressed in HSCs and HPCs than in mature blood cells (Yoshida et al., 2019)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yoshida et al., 2019.

claim: Lmo2 induces reprogramming of HSCs from differentiated blood cells and fibroblasts.
source: and is known to induce reprogramming of HSCs from differentiated blood cells (Riddell et al., 2014) and fibroblasts (Batta et al., 2014; Vereide et al., 2014)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: LMO2 actively contributes to the maintenance of the undifferentiated state of HSCs.
source: suggesting that LMO2 actively contributes to the maintenance of the undifferentiated state of HSCs
evidence: This is inferred from the high expression in HSCs/HPCs and reprogramming capacity.

claim: Aberrant induction of Lmo2 in thymocytes generates self-renewing cells that retain the capacity for T-cell differentiation.
source: Consistently, aberrant induction of Lmo2 in thymocytes generates self-renewing cells that retain the capacity for T-cell differentiation (McCormack et al., 2010; Cleveland et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from McCormack et al., 2010 and Cleveland et al., 2013.

claim: Pro-B cells without transcription factors essential for early B-cell development can be maintained in vitro with an HPC-like phenotype, retaining T-cell potential.
source: In attempts to establish HPC lines with T-cell differentiation potential, it has been found that pro-B cells without transcription factors essential for early B-cell development, including Pax5, Ebf1, and E2A (encoded by Tcf3), can be maintained in vitro with an HPC-like phenotype, retaining T-cell potential on OP9 stromal cells in the presence of IL-7 (Nutt et al., 1999; Rolink et al., 1999; Ikawa et al., 2004; Pongubala et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: Pro-B(+) cells were able to initiate differentiation into the T-cell lineage on OP9-Dll4 cells in vitro.
source: Pro-B(+) cells were able to initiate differentiation into the T-cell lineage, DN2 (CD25+CD44+), DN3 (CD25+CD44lo), and double-positive (DP) stages on Dll4-expressing OP9 (OP9-Dll4) cells in vitro (Figure 1A, lower right, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 1A.

claim: Pro-B(+) cells mature into CD4 and CD8 T cells in vivo.
source: and mature into CD4 and CD8 T cells in vivo (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: This is demonstrated by transplantation experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Pro-B(−) cells remained in the pro-B cell phenotype and died with Dll4-mediated Notch stimulation.
source: In contrast, pro-B(−) cells remained in the pro-B cell phenotype (CD25−CD44+B220int) and died with Dll4-mediated Notch stimulation
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A where pro-B(-) cells fail to differentiate and show reduced cell numbers.

claim: The expression levels of Notch receptors were comparable between pro-B(+) and pro-B(−) cells.
source: although the expression levels of the Notch receptors were comparable (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Approximately 400 differentially expressed genes (FC > 10) were identified between pro-B(+) and pro-B(−) cells.
source: We identified approximately 400 differentially expressed genes (FC > 10) between the pro-B(+) and pro-B(−) cells
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis comparing the two cell lines.

claim: Differentially expressed genes between pro-B(+) and pro-B(−) cells were enriched for genes related to the 'Hematopoietic cell lineage' pathway.
source: and these genes were enriched for genes related to the 'Hematopoietic cell lineage' pathway (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G)
evidence: This is based on KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The functional importance of Meis1, Hmga2, and Bcl11a has been reported in undifferentiated HPCs.
source: Among them, the functional importance of Meis1, Hmga2, and Bcl11a has been reported in undifferentiated HPCs (Wong et al., 2007; Ariki et al., 2014; Nishino et al., 2008; Copley et al., 2013; Yu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: Introduction of Meis1 and Hmga2 failed to overcome the defective T-cell differentiation in pro-B(−) cells in the presence of Notch signaling.
source: However, the introduction of Meis1 and Hmga2 failed to overcome the defective T-cell differentiation in the presence of Notch signaling
evidence: This is stated as a negative result from experiments testing these factors.

claim: Introduction of Bcl11a was highly toxic in pro-B(−) cells.
source: and that of Bcl11a was highly toxic in pro-B(−) cells (data not shown)
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation.

claim: The expression levels of Lmo2 mRNA were approximately threefold higher in pro-B(+) than pro-B(−) cells.
source: We found that the expression levels of Lmo2 mRNA and protein were approximately threefold higher in pro-B(+) than pro-B(−) cells (Figure 1B,C)
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR in Figure 1B.

claim: The expression levels of LMO2 protein were approximately threefold higher in pro-B(+) than pro-B(−) cells.
source: We found that the expression levels of Lmo2 mRNA and protein were approximately threefold higher in pro-B(+) than pro-B(−) cells (Figure 1B,C)
evidence: This is demonstrated by intracellular staining in Figure 1C.

claim: Enforced expression of Lmo2 markedly provided pro-B(−) cells with the capacity to differentiate into T-cell lineage following Notch stimulation in vitro.
source: and enforced expression of Lmo2 markedly provided their capacity to differentiate into T-cell lineage following Notch stimulation in vitro (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry in Figure 1D showing CD25+ cell generation.

claim: The ability of sgLMO2-treated BM progenitors to differentiate into the T-lineage was comparable to that of control.
source: The ability sgLMO2-treated progenitors to differentiate into the T-lineage was comparable to that of control (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: sgRNA against LMO2 caused specific loss of LMO2 protein 4 days after retroviral infection.
source: Cas9-introduced pro-B(+) cells were transduced with sgRNA against LMO2, which caused specific loss of LMO2 protein 4 days after retroviral infection as detected by immunoblotting (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblotting in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Lmo2-deficient pro-B(+) cells progressed to the DN2 stage as well as control cells on day 5 after sgRNA transduction.
source: Lmo2-deficient pro-B(+) cells progressed to the DN2 stage (CD25+CD44+) as well as control cells on day 5
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B (left panels).

claim: Developmental arrest was observed ten days after sgLMO2 transduction in pro-B(+) cells.
source: however, developmental arrest was observed ten days after sgLMO2 transduction (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B (right panels) where CD25+ cells are greatly reduced.

claim: Loss of T-cell differentiation potential took several days (~10 days) after Lmo2 disruption.
source: These results indicate that LMO2 is necessary for pro-B(+) cells to maintain their ability to differentiate into T-cell lineage, and loss of their differentiation potential took several days (~10 days) after Lmo2 disruption.
evidence: This is inferred from the time-course experiment in Figure 2B.

claim: The process of losing T-cell differentiation potential may require loss of LMO2-mediated slower time-scale transcriptional changes, including histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and DNA methylation.
source: Thus, the process may require loss of LMO2-mediated slower time-scale transcriptional changes, including histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and DNA methylation.
evidence: This is speculated based on the time course of phenotypic changes after Lmo2 deletion.

claim: Lmo2-introduction restored the expression of Bcl11a in pro-B(−) cells.
source: We found that Lmo2-introduction restored the expression of Bcl11a in pro-B(−) cells
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A by RT-qPCR.

claim: Meis1 further downregulated Bcl11a expression in pro-B(−) cells.
source: whereas Meis1 further downregulated Bcl11a expression
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A by RT-qPCR.

claim: Bcl11a regulates the survival of lymphoid progenitors via induction of the anti-apoptotic gene, Bcl2.
source: Bcl11a is known to regulate the survival of lymphoid progenitors via induction of the anti-apoptotic gene, Bcl2 (Yu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yu et al., 2012.

claim: Transduction of Bcl2 significantly protected pro-B(−) cells from cell death before and after Notch stimulation.
source: Transduction of Bcl2 significantly protected pro-B(−) cells from cell death, before and after Notch stimulation (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by Annexin V/7-AAD staining in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpression of Bcl11a was highly toxic in pro-B cells.
source: Conversly, overexpression of the oncogene, Bcl11a, was highly toxic in pro-B cells.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation.

claim: Bcl2-introduced pro-B(−) cells still failed to progress into the CD25+ DN2 stage.
source: Importantly, Bcl2-introduced pro-B(−) cells (pro-B(−)/Bcl2) still failed to progress into the CD25+ DN2 stage (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry in Figure 3C.

claim: LMO2 regulates survival of pro-B(−) cells via the Bcl11a/Bcl2 pathway.
source: Thus, these results suggest that LMO2 would regulate survival of pro-B(−) cells via the Bcl11a/Bcl2 pathway
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing Lmo2 regulates Bcl11a and Bcl2 rescues cell death.

claim: Other mechanisms besides the Bcl11a/Bcl2 pathway contribute to the maintenance of the potential to differentiate into T-cell lineage.
source: and other mechanisms contribute to the maintenance of the potential to differentiate into T-cell lineage
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that Bcl2 rescues survival but not differentiation potential.

claim: Expression of Tcf7 was weakly detected in pro-B(+) cells.
source: Our comparative microarray analysis of pro-B(−) and pro-B(+) cells showed that expression of Tcf7 (encoding TCF1), one of the most important and the earliest Notch target genes in thymic immigrant cells, was weakly detected in pro-B(+) cells
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis.

claim: Tcf7 expression level was approximately 100-fold lower in pro-B(−) cells compared to pro-B(+) cells.
source: however, its level was approximately 100-fold lower in pro-B(−) cells
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis.

claim: The upregulation of Tcf7 expression observed in pro-B(+)/Bcl2 cells after Notch stimulation was significantly abrogated in pro-B(−)/Bcl2 cells.
source: The upregulation of Tcf7 expression observed in pro-B(+)/Bcl2 cells after Notch stimulation was significantly abrogated in pro-B(−)/Bcl2 cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR in Figure 4A.

claim: Gata3 was upregulated by Notch stimulation but modestly lower in pro-B(−)/Bcl2 cells compared to pro-B(+)/Bcl2 cells.
source: In contrast, another Notch-regulated gene, Gata3, was upregulated by Notch stimulation but modestly lower in pro-B(−)/Bcl2 cells compared to that in pro-B(+)/Bcl2 cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR in Figure 4A.

claim: TCF1 and GATA3 protein expression differences between pro-B(+)/Bcl2 and pro-B(−)/Bcl2 cells were confirmed at 7 days post-Notch stimulation.
source: These results were further confirmed at the protein level using pro-B(−)/Bcl2 and pro-B(+)/Bcl2 cells at 7 days post-Notch stimulation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by intracellular staining in Figure 4B.

claim: There was a decrease in Tcf7 expression in Lmo2-deficient pro-B(+) cells after 10 days but not after 5 days of sgRNA transduction.
source: In addition, there was a decrease in Tcf7 expression in Lmo2-deficient pro-B(+) cells (Figure 2) after 10 days but not after 5 days of sgRNA transduction (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Introduction of Tcf7 clearly rescued the defect in the differentiation capacity of pro-B(−)/Bcl2 into T-cell lineage after Notch signaling.
source: We then tested the role of Tcf7 using a gain-of-function strategy and found that introduction of Tcf7 clearly rescued the defect in the differentiation capacity of pro-B(−)/Bcl2 into T-cell lineage (DN2 stage), after Notch signaling was provided (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry in Figure 4C.

claim: LMO2 expression in T-cell progenitors plays a crucial role in the activation of Tcf7 once the progenitors migrate into the thymus and are stimulated by Notch signaling.
source: These results indicate that LMO2 expression in T-cell progenitors plays a crucial role in the activation of Tcf7 once the progenitors migrate into the thymus and are stimulated by Notch signaling.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing LMO2 is required for Tcf7 activation and Tcf7 rescues differentiation.

claim: In pro-B(+) cells, the transcriptional start site of the Tcf7 locus was highly enriched for the active histone mark H3K4-3Me.
source: We observed that in pro-B(+) cells, the transcriptional start site (TSS) of the Tcf7 locus was highly enriched for the active histone mark H3K4-3Me.
evidence: This is shown by ChIP analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Lmo2 disruption caused a significant reduction in the H3K4-3Me marks 10 days post-sgRNA introduction (~30%).
source: However, Lmo2 disruption caused a significant reduction in the H3K4-3Me marks 10 days post-sgRNA introduction (~30%)
evidence: This is shown by ChIP analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Lmo2 disruption caused a modest reduction in the H3K4-3Me levels after 5 days of Lmo2 deletion (~70%).
source: and a modest reduction in the H3K4-3Me levels after 5 days of Lmo2 deletion (~70%) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is shown by ChIP analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: A CpG island exists at the TSSs of Tcf7.
source: Moreover, we found a CpG island at the TSSs of Tcf7 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In pro-B(−) cells, the CpG island at the Tcf7 locus was highly methylated (77.6%).
source: In pro-B(−) cells, the CpG island at the Tcf7 locus was highly methylated, in contrast to pro-B(+) cells that had a highly demethylated TSSs (77.6% vs. 29.8%) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown by bisulfite sequencing in Figure 5B.

claim: In pro-B(+) cells, the CpG island at the Tcf7 locus was highly demethylated (29.8%).
source: In pro-B(−) cells, the CpG island at the Tcf7 locus was highly methylated, in contrast to pro-B(+) cells that had a highly demethylated TSSs (77.6% vs. 29.8%) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown by bisulfite sequencing in Figure 5B.

claim: Enforced expression of Lmo2 in pro-B(−) cells induced demethylation of the CpG island at the TSSs of Tcf7.
source: Moreover, enforced expression of Lmo2 in pro-B(−) cells induced demethylation of the CpG island at the TSSs (Figure 5B, pro-B(−)/LMO2).
evidence: This is shown by bisulfite sequencing in Figure 5B.

claim: The epigenetic status of the Tcf7 locus in the progenitor cells is maintained by LMO2 in a transcriptionally poised chromatin state for quick responsiveness following Notch stimulation.
source: These results demonstrate that the epigenetic status of the Tcf7 locus in the progenitor cells is maintained by LMO2 in a transcriptionally poised chromatin state for quick responsiveness following Notch stimulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing LMO2 maintains demethylation and H3K4-3Me at the Tcf7 locus.

claim: More than 1500 reproducible LMO2 binding peaks were identified in pro-B(+) cells.
source: We identified more than 1500 reproducible LMO2 binding peaks
evidence: This is based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: Runx and ETS motifs are enriched in LMO2 binding sites.
source: and enrichment of Runx and ETS motifs that are frequently found in open chromatin regions of hematopoietic progenitors and pre-commitment pro-T cells (Yoshida et al., 2019; Ungerbäck et al., 2018; Figure 6A)
evidence: This is shown by motif analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: The motif for bHLH factors was coenriched in LMO2 binding sites.
source: The motif for a previously reported LMO2 interacting partner, the bHLH factors, was also coenriched (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is shown by motif analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: Many bHLH-regulated genes, including Lyl1, Erg, and Hhex, were bound by LMO2.
source: Many of the bHLH-regulated genes, including Lyl1, Erg, and Hhex, were bound by LMO2 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is shown by ChIP-seq tracks in Figure 6B.

claim: A clear LMO2 peak was observed at the −35 kb upstream region of the Tcf7 locus.
source: Most importantly, a clear LMO2 peak was observed at the −35 kb upstream region of the Tcf7 locus.
evidence: This is shown by ChIP-seq tracks in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The LMO2 binding site at −35 kb upstream of Tcf7 overlapped with RBPJ binding sites.
source: This binding site overlapped with RBPJ, a DNA-binding subunit of the Notch intracellular domain (NICD) transcriptional complex, binding sites at the Tcf7 locus, and co-occupied with Runx1 in pre-commitment DN1 cells (GSE148441, GSE110020) (Romero-Wolf et al., 2020; Hosokawa et al., 2018; Shin et al., 2021; Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by comparing ChIP-seq tracks in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The LMO2 binding site at −35 kb upstream of Tcf7 was co-occupied with Runx1 in pre-commitment DN1 cells.
source: This binding site overlapped with RBPJ, a DNA-binding subunit of the Notch intracellular domain (NICD) transcriptional complex, binding sites at the Tcf7 locus, and co-occupied with Runx1 in pre-commitment DN1 cells (GSE148441, GSE110020) (Romero-Wolf et al., 2020; Hosokawa et al., 2018; Shin et al., 2021; Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by comparing ChIP-seq tracks in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: LMO2 directly binds to the Bcl11a and Tcf7 loci and regulates their expression to maintain the ability of progenitors to differentiate into T-cell lineage.
source: Taken together, LMO2 directly binds to the Bcl11a and Tcf7 loci and regulates their expression to maintain the ability of progenitors to differentiate into T-cell lineage.
evidence: This is the main conclusion integrating ChIP-seq data with functional studies.

claim: TD7 is a thymic stromal cell line established from fetal thymus.
source: TD7, thymic stromal cell line established from fetal thymus (B6, embryonic day 15.5)
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: TD7 cells seem to be derived from thymic mesenchymal cells as they express PDGFRα.
source: These cell line seems to be derived from thymic mesenchymal cells as they express PDGFRα.

claim: TD7 can support B-cell differentiation.
source: The stromal cell line TD7 can support B-cell differentiation.

claim: Lin+ cells are generated more frequently on TD7 than on OP9 monolayers.
source: Lin+ cells are generated more frequently on TD7 than on OP9 monolayers.

claim: Pro-B(−) and pro-B(+) cells express intermediate levels of B220.
source: Pro-B(−) and pro-B(+) cells express intermediate levels of B220.

claim: LMO2 acts as a gatekeeper for maintaining the transcriptionally poised chromatin state of the Tcf7 locus via direct binding to the −35 kb region.
source: Taken together, in the T-cell progenitor stage, LMO2 acts as a gatekeeper for maintaining the transcriptionally poised chromatin state of the Tcf7 locus via direct binding to the −35 kb region, and guarantees T-cell differentiation potential.
evidence: This is the main mechanistic conclusion of the study integrating multiple lines of evidence.

claim: LMO2 guarantees T-cell differentiation potential.
source: Taken together, in the T-cell progenitor stage, LMO2 acts as a gatekeeper for maintaining the transcriptionally poised chromatin state of the Tcf7 locus via direct binding to the −35 kb region, and guarantees T-cell differentiation potential.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The functional importance of the −31 kb region has been previously reported as a Notch-dependent enhancer of Tcf7.
source: Among these, the functional importance of the −31 kb region has been previously reported as a Notch-dependent enhancer of Tcf7 (Weber et al., 2011; Harly et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Weber et al., 2011 and Harly et al., 2020.

claim: Two NICD-RBPJ complex and Runx1 binding sites were found at the −31 and −35 kb upstream regions of the Tcf7 locus.
source: Two NICD-RBPJ complex and Runx1 binding sites were found at the −31 and −35 kb upstream regions of the Tcf7 locus (Figure 6—figure supplement 1; Weber et al., 2011; Romero-Wolf et al., 2020; Hosokawa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and cited from previous studies.

claim: Initiation of Tcf7 expression requires Notch signaling and Runx factors in T-cell progenitors.
source: Initiation of Tcf7 expression requires Notch signaling and Runx factors in T-cell progenitors (Weber et al., 2011; Guo et al., 2008; Shin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: LMO2 forms complexes with bHLH transcription factors, including E2A, Lyl1, and TAL1/SCL.
source: Previous reports suggest that LMO2 forms complexes with the bHLH transcription factors, including E2A, Lyl1, and TAL1/SCL, and binds to their target genomic sites (Wadman et al., 1997; Grütz et al., 1998; El Omari et al., 2013; Layer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: The binding motif for bHLH factors was enriched in LMO2 binding regions in pro-B(+) cells.
source: Consistently, in this study, we found that the binding motif for bHLH factors was enriched in LMO2 binding regions in pro-B(+) cells.
evidence: This is shown by motif analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: LMO2 functions along with bHLH factors in lymphoid progenitors.
source: Thus, LMO2 seems to function along with these bHLH factors in the lymphoid progenitors.
evidence: This is inferred from the enrichment of bHLH motifs in LMO2 binding sites.

claim: Lmo2 expression levels were associated with DNA methylation status around the Tcf7 locus.
source: In fact, Lmo2 expression levels were found to be associated with DNA methylation status around the Tcf7 locus and subsequent Notch-mediated activation of Tcf7 expression.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing methylation status in pro-B(-), pro-B(+), and pro-B(-)/LMO2 cells in Figure 5B.

claim: Lmo2 expression levels were associated with subsequent Notch-mediated activation of Tcf7 expression.
source: In fact, Lmo2 expression levels were found to be associated with DNA methylation status around the Tcf7 locus and subsequent Notch-mediated activation of Tcf7 expression.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing Tcf7 expression after Notch stimulation in pro-B(+)/Bcl2 and pro-B(-)/Bcl2 cells in Figure 4A.

claim: As the Tcf7 locus remains in an accessible state in HPCs or lineage-committed cells with ectopic LMO2 expression, they efficiently differentiate into T-lineage cells and selectively develop T-cell malignancy.
source: Therefore, it can be inferred that, as the Tcf7 locus remains in an accessible state in HPCs or lineage-committed cells with ectopic LMO2 expression, they efficiently differentiate into T-lineage cells and selectively develop T-cell malignancy.
evidence: This is speculated based on the findings about LMO2's role in maintaining Tcf7 accessibility.

claim: TCF1 forms a complex with β-catenin, which contributes to the development of T-cell malignancy.
source: In addition, TCF1 forms a complex with β-catenin, which contributes to the development of T-cell malignancy (Bigas et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Bigas et al., 2020.

claim: The β-catenin/TCF1 complex, together with RAG molecules, induces various genetic instabilities including those in the Myc gene in immature T cells and causes Myc gene-targeted tumorigenesis.
source: Although the contribution of the β-catenin/TCF1 complex in normal T-cell development remains unclear, the complex, together with RAG molecules, induces various genetic instabilities including those in the Myc gene in immature T cells and causes Myc gene-targeted tumorigenesis (Dose et al., 2014; Gekas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Dose et al., 2014 and Gekas et al., 2016.

claim: TCF1 is involved in other tumorigenesis besides T-cell malignancy.
source: As TCF1 is also involved in other tumorigenesis (Liu et al., 2019)

source: These results suggest that TD7 does not support the pluripotency of Ebf1-deficient pro-B cells, leading to loss of LMO2.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that pro-B cells cultured on TD7 have lower LMO2 and lose T-cell potential.

claim: Several cis-regulatory elements around the Lmo2 locus cooperatively function and ensure the full expression pattern of Lmo2.
source: Although the molecular machinery underlying LMO2 expression in HSCs has not been fully described, it was shown that several cis-regulatory elements around the Lmo2 locus cooperatively function and ensure the full expression pattern of Lmo2 (Landry et al., 2005; Landry et al., 2009)

claim: Lmo2 expression is driven in part by PU.1, TAL1, GATA factors, and LMO2 itself.
source: which appears to be driven in part by PU.1, TAL1, GATA factors, and LMO2 itself

claim: The culture conditions provided by TD7 may be unable to sustain sufficient expression of transcription factors that regulate Lmo2.

evidence: This is speculated as a possible mechanism for lower LMO2 in TD7-cultured cells.

evidence: This is speculated as an alternative mechanism, with citation to Nakano et al., 1994 about OP9 not producing M-CSF.

claim: The establishment of pro-B cells on TD7 was accompanied by a prolonged emergence of myeloid marker-positive cells compared to that on OP9.
source: In fact, the establishment of pro-B cells on TD7 was accompanied by a prolonged emergence of myeloid marker-positive cells compared to that on OP9

claim: HSCs may be depleted by differentiation into the myeloid lineage on TD7, resulting in IL-7-dependent proliferation of pro-B cells without pluripotency that express reduced Lmo2.
source: Therefore, HSCs may be depleted by differentiation into the myeloid lineage, resulting in IL-7-dependent proliferation of pro-B cells without pluripotency that express reduced Lmo2.
evidence: This is speculated as a mechanism for the establishment of pro-B(-) cells on TD7.

source: In either case, substantial expression of Lmo2 is critical for the maintenance of pluripotency in Ebf1-deficient pro-B cells
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that LMO2 levels correlate with T-cell potential.
